title: feat(types): declare the seven data-table handler keys its renderer reads (objectui#7804 DataTableSchema slice)
body:
Part of #7804 — the `DataTableSchema` slice. Seven of that card's ledger rows drain here; **29 remain** and are later slices, so this PR deliberately carries no closing keyword. The PM seat ends the card when the last row is gone.

## What changed

`BaseSchema` is `.passthrough()`, so a key no arm declares is **not refused** — it stops being judged and the value is KEPT, then reaches the renderer that reads it. Seven `DataTableSchema` keys sat in exactly that state while `renderers/complex/data-table.tsx` read and INVOKED each one, so an authored `{ "type": "data-table", "onRowClick": { "action": "toast" } }` parsed GREEN and that action object was handed to a call site expecting a function.

Each is now a `handlerKeyRefusal(key, 'runtime-slot', label)` arm on `data-display.zod.ts#DataTableSchema`, beside the four (`onRowEdit`, `onRowDelete`, `onSelectionChange`, `onColumnsReorder`) that already carried the same shape.

## The deliverable: a MEASURED disposition per key, not a pattern applied seven times

`'retired'` publishes *"no renderer reads this key, so nothing could ever run it"* — flatly false for all seven, since this card's premise is that a registered renderer reads them. So the burden was on `'runtime-slot'`, which asserts a host really supplies the function through the TypeScript interface / props. Found per key, by the props path:

| key | read site (cited by content) | who supplies it | disposition |
|---|---|---|---|
| `onAddRecord` | `onClick={() => schema.onAddRecord?.()}` | `ObjectGrid` forwards `ObjectGridComponentProps.onAddRecord`; hosts `ObjectManager`, `FieldDesigner` fill it | `runtime-slot` |
| `onBatchSave` | `await schema.onBatchSave(changesToSave)` | `ObjectGrid`'s `onBatchSave ?? defaultBatchSave` — left limb is the React prop | `runtime-slot` |
| `onCellChange` | `schema.onCellChange(globalIndex, columnKey, valueToStage, row)` | `ObjectGrid` forwards the React prop of the same name | `runtime-slot` |
| `onColumnResize` | `schema.onColumnResize?.(resizedColumn, finalWidth)` | ⚠️ **no host prop anywhere** — `ObjectGrid` supplies its OWN closure and reports the merged `{ order, widths }` layout to its host through `onColumnStateChange` instead | `runtime-slot` |
| `onRowActionDef` | `onActionDef={schema.onRowActionDef}` | `RelatedList` forwards its own `onRowAction` React prop | `runtime-slot` |
| `onRowClick` | `schema.onRowClick(row)`, gated on `!e.defaultPrevented` | THREE suppliers: `ObjectGrid` (`navigation.handleClick`), `ObjectDataTable` (`schema.onRowClick ?? handleRowClick`), `RelatedList` (its own prop) | `runtime-slot` |
| `onRowSave` | `await schema.onRowSave(globalIndex, rowChanges, row)` | `ObjectGrid`'s `onRowSave ?? defaultRowSave` — left limb is the React prop | `runtime-slot` |

⭐ **`onColumnResize` is the one that made the per-key rule pay.** It is the only one of the seven with no React prop carrying it on any component: `ObjectGrid` supplies a closure of its own, because the table vocabulary is per-event and the grid's persisted vocabulary is the merged blob. Read off its six siblings it would still have landed `runtime-slot`, but for the wrong reason; read as `'retired'` it would have published a false sentence for a read objectui#6175 wired on purpose. A live function does reach the renderer through the TypeScript face, so the slot is real and the disposition holds.

⚠️ **No key came out "read but supplied by nothing".** That third outcome is the one the dispatch asked to be reported rather than forced into the nearer box; it did not occur here.

## The breaking-change question — measured, with a lit control

This narrows a published accept set, so the census had to be a reading and not a silence.

| corpus | files | the seven, JSON key spelling | lit control on the same corpus |
|---|---|---|---|
| all tracked `.json` / `.md` / `.mdx` / `.yml` / `.yaml` | 2602 | **0** for every one | `"searchable"` 5 files · `"pageSize"` 11 · `"exportable"` 3 · `"columns"` 74 |
| `apps/` + `examples/` TypeScript sources | 274 | **0** (the single `onRowClick` hit is a React prop on a `ListView` element in a console preview, not an authored document) | `searchable` 4 · `pageSize` 1 · `columns` 33 |
| `examples/schema-catalog` | 471 | **0** for every one | `data-table` 6 |

Every textual hit on these names anywhere in the tree is **prose** — changeset history, CHANGELOG entries and `plugin-grid` docs describing them as React props. Nothing authors any of the seven as metadata. ⇒ the changeset declares `minor` with the narrowing stated in full; per this repo's fixed-group rule a `major` is not available and breaking semantics are carried in the body.

## Is `KNOWN_UNDECLARED_READS` generated or hand-maintained?

**Hand-maintained.** Stated explicitly because it was a live confusion on the sibling card objectui#7265. Measured, not assumed: the constant is a literal `new Map([...])` in `scripts/check-handler-key-read-sites.mjs`, the file carries no `@generated` / `DO NOT EDIT` marker, no script writes it, there is no `gen:*` npm script in this repo at all, and the only other references to the name are the gate's own reads and its test importing the exported Map. So the seven rows were deleted by hand, which is the sanctioned path — not a hand-edit of a generated block.

## Evidence

**Directions predicted in writing before running.** Both predictions held.

**P1 — the INTERMEDIATE reading (arm declared, ledger row NOT yet removed).** Predicted RED on `staleExemptions()`. Measured: `EXIT=1`, naming exactly the seven —

```
x  7 KNOWN_UNDECLARED_READS row(s) name a read site this gate no longer finds:
      data-table::DataTableSchema.onAddRecord
      ... (all seven)
The defect the row waives is gone, so the row is now a live waiver for nothing. Delete it.
```

That is the proof the arm edit reached these exact keys.

**P2 — ABLATION (arms reverted, ledger left drained).** Predicted RED the OTHER way. Measured: `EXIT=1`, all seven reported as undeclared reads with no row to exempt them (`DataTableSchema (data-display.zod.ts) does not declare it.`). Two opposite reds out of one gate is what shows the arm edit and the ledger drain are each load-bearing for the other.

- **Mutation proven on disk**, both ways: the `handlerKeyRefusal(` anchor count inside the `DataTableSchema` block went `11 → 4`, AND the on-disk blob hash equalled the base blob (`edab1edb…`) exactly.
- **Restore proven by state**, not by an exit code: blob hash back to the HEAD blob (`bf07d9dd…`), `git diff HEAD` empty, `git status --porcelain` empty.
- The whole leg ran under `trap ... EXIT INT TERM` with absolute paths, and empty hashes were treated as FAILURE rather than as "nothing to compare".
- No build step is involved: this gate parses `packages/types/src/zod/*.zod.ts` from **source** through the TypeScript AST, so there is no `dist/` layer that could keep a mutation alive or hide one.

**After the drain**, the gate is green and prints its own count:

```
OK  105 arm(s), 212 registration(s) (119 with an arm), 60 reachable handler read(s),
    60 judged, 0 left unjudged ..., 29 exempted by ledger
```

Ledger re-derived at this branch point rather than quoted: 36 rows before, 29 after — with a live control, since the pattern that matches rows (`['type::Schema.onX', 'objectui#7804'],`) reads 36 over the Map and 0 over the docblock above it.

## Gates run locally

| gate | verdict |
|---|---|
| `check:handler-key-reads` | exit 0 (green after the drain; red in both ablation legs, as designed) |
| `zod-mirror-parity` + `handler-keys-json-refusal-6124` | exit 0 — `Test Files 2 passed (2)`, `Tests 328 passed (328)` |
| `@object-ui/types` `type-check` (3 tsconfigs) | exit 0, under the shared verify lock |
| `check:control-bytes` | exit 0 — 7715 tracked text files scanned |
| `check:new-line-citations` | exit 0 — 0 new cross-file line citations added by this branch |
| changeset presence / no-major / claims | exit 0 / exit 0 / exit 0 |

Ledger moves the two pinned ledgers required, all of them derived and none carried in from a card: `RUNTIME_SLOT` 44 → 51 and the site total 65 → 72 in `handler-keys-json-refusal-6124.test.ts`; `KnownDrift` key total 65 → 72 and `RuntimeOnlyDeclared` key total 24 → 17 in `zod-mirror-parity.test.ts`, entry counts unchanged in both because the keys moved **between existing entries for the same pair**. That asymmetry (key totals move, entry counts do not) is what the parity file's own failure text says to expect for a transfer.

## Acceptance notes

Out-of-scope observations, noted and NOT filed:

- The `RuntimeOnlyDeclared` entry for this pair survives with five keys — `onColumnReorder`, `onPageChange`, `onPageSizeChange`, `onSearchChange`, `onSortChange`. They are **not** a follow-on of this slice and are deliberately untouched: four are host-driven pagination/sort/search slots, and `onColumnReorder` is the open one-event-two-spellings ruling objectui#6175 explicitly declined to settle. Successor: whoever takes that ruling.
- The running tally in `handler-keys-json-refusal-6124.test.ts`'s file header (`36 sites … 40 since …`) had never carried objectui#7655's six or objectui#8802's removals, so it was already not today's figure. Repaired opportunistically in a file this PR touches anyway: it now says so and points at the length pin instead of gaining another digit. Not filed — no gate reads it, and it is now self-describing.

## Landing

Draft, and it stays draft: not enqueued, no auto-merge armed. `needs:contract-review` is on it because the claim comment declares `Clause-②: yes` — adding an arm to a published mirror is a declaration change, and this one is a NARROWING.
